title: R09 public-community — the anonymous comment pipeline and its staff moderation gate
why: Twenty rows across a PHP edge relay, the Python bot, a NestJS controller/service/contract, a Postgres migration, a retention action, a deployed Next.js chunk, a PWA moderation queue, and one retirement ratchet split over two files — the guard `package5_public_community_runtime_guard.py` (S-709) and the frozen r09 contract it consumes, `package5_wave_rc_guard_contracts.py` (S-725); that is one mechanism in two files, not two independent defences. Signing this group names one canonical owner for the whole pipeline — `PublicCommunityService` on the NestJS backend — and the code already behaves that way: the SQLite writers in `site_engagement` are retired body by body, the AI-moderation and brand-reply authority they once held is gone, and `canonical_public_community` is demoted to an HMAC signing source that structurally cannot carry a tenant, User or Client. What the inventory lacked was the row saying so — all twenty rows carry `canonicalOwner: —` with `canonicalOwnerSource: REQUIRES SIGNATURE`. Two of them (S-709, S-725) also carry an unsigned successor cell, `CLASS_S_DESTINATION — one of the five, to be named`, so signing this group as attribution still leaves those two destinations unnamed.
disappear: Nothing disappears on signature: this group names an owner and changes no code. The one retirement the rows carry is not authorised here — `site_engagement` (S-707) is marked RETIRE IN K16 only after a recorded unreachability probe, a probe and not an assumption, and its already-retired bodies stay AST-frozen meanwhile, so it is not a free deletion. The ten rows reading RETIRE FROM PRIMARY NAV — K16 remove nothing from navigation today: every one of them is already `primaryNav: false`. The single primary-nav row in the group, the PWA moderation queue, is not retired at all.
remain: The HMAC source-signing boundary end to end — the edge gateway minting and signing the pseudonymous `me_visitor` subject, the ±90 s verification window, the operation allowlist — and the tenant fence that resolves tenant only from the configured gateway mapping, never from the request. The consent rule at the canonical owner: `acceptComment` refuses the write unless `publicationConsent` is explicitly given, and records an append-only anonymous GUEST consent fact with no Client or User foreign key by design. The text/author safety contract that normalises input, collapses every author to «Гость» and rejects PII, profanity and staff impersonation. Likes and daily views stay per-browser-scope facts, explicitly not per-person counts. The split between source and moderator: moderation and brand reply stay behind a role gate — @Roles plus current active exact-tenant membership, a role gate and not separation of duties — with the PWA queue «Обсуждения на сайте» kept as a fullscreen secondary, its query-param door (`?community_moderation`, no route_key) recorded as a defect; K5 assigns the real route key, and the entry mechanism still waits on decision D4. The 365-day payload retention purge, the frozen retirement contract and its runtime guard, and the public site community UI on muzhskayaestetika.рф, which stays out of scope with no source in this repository.
risk: LOW-MEDIUM. LOW as an attribution: it names an owner the code already behaves like, no implementation follows in Wave 1, and what the step adds is evidence rather than behaviour. It is not plain LOW because part of the twenty cannot be read here. Three rows carry the conflict-C4 caveat — S-722 has no file and zero grep matches and is recorded UNRESOLVED IN THIS CHECKOUT; S-721 is absent and rests on a production sha256; S-724 is present but `grep -c "api/site"` returns 0, so the community and guest routes are not registered in the checked-out bootstrap while the production inventory says the modules run — and a fourth, the Beget dispatcher (S-720), is read only as a sanitized fixture of a production-only file. All three C4 rows are themselves class OUT OF SCOPE and NOT RETIRED, so the signature authorises nothing over them; the sting is S-724's finding, which puts in doubt whether the in-scope anonymous ingress route (S-706) is registered at all in the artefact this checkout holds. That is a question for the CAPABILITY owner, not a reason to withhold the attribution. The re-pointing hazard — someone reading "canonical owner: NestJS" as licence to re-point the Python writers — is real and only partly mechanical: the ratchet AST-compares the retired `site_community` / `site_engagement` bodies enumerated in the frozen r09 contract, so those named bodies cannot be revived unnoticed, but a Python writer added outside the frozen set is not blocked by it, and the ratchet's own protection ("must never be relaxed", "must not be edited to accommodate a UX change") is a norm held by review, not an enforced rule.
user_impact: No user notices anything from this decision: O01 is owner-attribution and changes no code in Wave 1. Only 2 of its 20 rows render anything to a person — S-718 and S-719; the other 18 are a Beget PHP relay, HMAC signing gateways, a NestJS controller/service/contract, a Postgres migration, a 365-day payload-retention purge, the fenced legacy SQLite store and the AST guard with its frozen contract (S-703, S-706, S-707, S-708, S-709, S-710, S-711, S-712, S-713, S-714, S-715, S-716, S-717, S-720, S-721, S-722, S-724, S-725). The only row a person touches inside MAYA's own app is S-719, the moderation queue «Обсуждения на сайте», gated to an authenticated owner/admin holding moderation rights on that business. The defect on that row must be stated correctly, because the fix depends on it: the queue is not a registered screen at all — `setTimeout(openMayaCommunityModeration,0)` (app.html:33069) appends a fixed full-screen overlay to document.body when `?community_moderation` is present, entirely outside the __meGo screen registry. And it is not merely un-linked: app.html:33983 still renders `Обсуждения на сайте`, but inside the second `AStaffDashboard` (app.html:33324), which never mounts because `window.ALivePanel` (app.html:37629) wins the `panel:` slot at app.html:39152. So a hand-typed query param is indeed the only live door today, but what K5 inherits is a DEAD menu entry plus a missing route_key, not an absent link. K5 owns that fix (a real route_key plus a chat summary card with HANDOFF), and the row records that the entry mechanism still depends on unresolved decision D4 — it is queued behind a decision, not scheduled. The anonymous visitor leaving a comment sees no change either: that UI is S-718, browser JS injected into a deployed Next.js chunk on muzhskayaestetika.рф with no source in this repository, a separate web property recorded as out of scope for the chat-first shell (conflicts C3/C4).
security_impact: NONE in direction — no check is added, removed or relocated, because the group writes an owner name onto rows whose code is untouched. What it does is put in writing the fences the rows already show, each of which verifies in this checkout: tenant is taken only from the configured gateway mapping and never from the request body, with a per-gateway secret and a ±90 s signature window (public-community-gateway.service.ts L99-120, L139; S-710, S-711); moderation and brand reply sit behind @TenantScoped plus @Roles(TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN, ADMINISTRATOR) with current active exact-tenant membership (S-714); and acceptComment throws ForbiddenException unless publicationConsent is explicitly true with a versioned policy string, writing an anonymous GUEST fact whose table carries FKs only to Tenant, the parent comment and ActionExecution — no Client or User FK (S-712, S-716), with a 365-day retentionUntil enforced by a DB CHECK (migration L82) and purged by nulling the encrypted payload (S-717). Two limits must travel with that list or it reads stronger than it is. First, S-714 is an APPROVAL path, and the envelope's Part 7 §5 leaves the four-eyes gap OPEN: approval here is role-gated, NOT separation of duties — four roles share the gate and the same account that approves a comment can also post the brand reply. O01 changes none of that, and naming a canonical owner must not be read as closing it. Second, the mechanical guarantee this group leans on — the AST ratchet (S-709) and its frozen contract (S-725) keeping the Python writers fenced — is proven against THIS checkout only: site_publications.py (S-721) and site_publication_bot.py (S-722) do not exist here, the real Beget api-proxy.php survives only as a sanitized fixture (S-720), and `grep -c "api/site"` returns 0 in webhook_server.py (S-724), so the community routes are unregistered here while the production inventory says the modules run (conflict C4). Which Python artefact is actually deployed is unknown to this cycle. The residual exposure is therefore documentary AND unverified-in-production: the phrase "canonical owner: NestJS" could later be misread as licence to re-point the Python writers, and the ratchet that would stop that is demonstrated only where the code can be read. Note also that the group is not purely owner-attribution: S-709 and S-725 each still carry an unsigned successor cell ("CLASS_S_DESTINATION — one of the five, to be named").
